title: The Typewriter of the Lower Danube
premise: In 1938, in a river town on the Lower Danube, Astrid Dravenmoor is completing the atlas her master died for when a stranger arrives carrying pages in the master's unmistakable handwriting — proof he is alive, and that his final maps document something powerful men want erased. To finish the atlas and honor both loyalty and truth, Astrid must smuggle the evidence past three checkpoints downriver before the border closes. Along the way she learns her master's survival was bought with a betrayal that touches her own family. In the end she chooses truth over safety, publishing the atlas under both their names and paying the price of exile — but not silence.
about_author: O. M. Vane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing border-town records along the Danube before turning to fiction. Vane writes historical thrillers about ordinary people caught between memory and power.

chapters.title: The Unfinished Coastline
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. In the mapmaker's attic studio, Astrid inks the final plates of Master Herron's atlas, telling herself history happens elsewhere. She finds one coastline deliberately left blank and a locked drawer she was never given the key to. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ferry Landing
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. A rain-soaked stranger named Ilya arrives asking for Herron by name — though Herron drowned two years ago. He produces a letter in the master's hand, dated last month. Emotional beat: the ground tilts; grief becomes suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Blank Space Hid
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Ilya reveals the blank coastline conceals fortified positions Herron mapped before vanishing, and that men in the capital are burning every copy. He needs Astrid's knowledge of the river checkpoints. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged over shared fear.

chapters.title: The First Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Disguised as a survey crew, they pass the first checkpoint by bribing an old colleague of Herron's — who then quietly reports them. Astrid realizes loyalty cuts both ways. Emotional beat: first taste of complicity and its cost.

chapters.title: Letters from a Drowned Man
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Reading Herron's smuggled letters, Astrid learns he survived by informing on fellow mapmakers — possibly including her father. Her faith in the man she mourns curdles. Emotional beat: betrayal discovered inside devotion.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Dinner
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Cornered at a riverside inn, Astrid is invited to dine with the checkpoint colonel, who knows exactly who she is and offers her safety in exchange for the letters. She lies beautifully and hates herself for how easily it comes. Emotional beat: power seduces; corruption begins at the table.

chapters.title: The Second Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The second checkpoint nearly breaks them; Ilya takes a beating covering Astrid's escape with the plates hidden in her coat lining. His confession: he was the one who sold Herron out, and has been trying to undo it since. Emotional beat: guilt as penance, trust rebuilt through wounds.

chapters.title: The Burning of the Archive
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reaching the capital's print quarter, they find the archive where the atlas plates were stored already ablaze — the colonel arrived first. Astrid saves a single proof copy from the fire. Emotional beat: despair transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Third Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. At the border, the colonel waits personally. Herron himself appears — alive, compromised, offering to trade the truth for Astrid's safe passage. Astrid refuses the bargain, exposes the fortifications publicly using the proof copy, and forces the guards' hands. Emotional beat: the choice between survival and truth made at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Atlas of Both Names
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue tone. Exiled but unbroken, Astrid publishes the completed atlas abroad under both names — hers and the master's, betrayer and betrayed bound in ink. She draws the once-blank coastline complete. Emotional beat: costly peace; truth survives its keepers.
